title: A Conditional Probability Is Still a Probability
quickIdea: Fix B and read P(.|B) as a new probability measure. It satisfies the three axioms, so the complement rule, the addition rule and monotonicity all survive inside the condition - and only inside it.
remember: For a fixed B with P(B) > 0 the function A -> P(A|B) is a probability measure: P(A|B) >= 0, P(whole space|B) = 1, and disjoint events add. NPTEL Lecture 09 proves all three from the axioms.
So P(A^c|B) = 1 - P(A|B), P(A or C|B) = P(A|B) + P(C|B) - P(A and C|B), and A contained in C gives P(A|B) <= P(C|B).
P(B|B) = 1 and P(nothing|B) = 0 for every B with positive probability.
Different conditions are different measures. P(A|B) + P(A|B^c) need not be 1; for a die with A = {2} and B = even it is 1/3 + 0 = 1/3.
Conditional probabilities with different conditions cannot be added into an unconditional probability. The total probability theorem is the rule that does that job, and it uses weights.
The ordinary set algebra applies to the events before conditioning: A and B^c = A minus (A and B), and A^c and B^c = (A or B)^c. Most 'given' questions are solved by that algebra plus one division.

example.prompt: A fair die is rolled and B = {2, 4, 6}. Find P({1,2}|B), P({1,3,5}|B) and P({2,4}|B).
example.work: Inside B the three outcomes are equally likely. {1,2} meets B in {2}, so P({1,2}|B) = 1/3. {1,3,5} meets B in nothing, so the probability is 0. {2,4} is contained in B, so its probability is 2/3. The three values 1/3, 0, 2/3 are exactly what the axioms demand of a probability measure on a three-point space.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2024 Set 1 Q.17 is set algebra rather than conditioning, and it is the algebra every conditional solution uses: P(A or B) by inclusion-exclusion, P(A and B^c) = P(A) - P(A and B), and P(A^c and B^c) = 1 - P(A or B).

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2024 Set 1 Q.17 (Q.27 in the official paper): P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.5, P(A and B) = 0.1. Which are true? (A) A and B are independent. (B) P(A or B) = 0.7. (C) P(A and B^c) = 0.2. (D) P(A^c and B^c) = 0.4.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: For a die with A = {2} and B = even, compute P(A|B) + P(A|B^c) and say why the sum is not 1.
variations.why: P(.|B) and P(.|B^c) are two different measures on two different spaces. The complement rule relates A to A^c inside one fixed condition; it never relates two different conditions.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: If P(A|B) = 0.3 and P(A and B) = 0.12, what is P(B)?
variations.why: Rearrange the definition: P(B) = P(A and B)/P(A|B) = 0.12/0.3 = 0.4. GATE has not asked this inversion in a CSE paper, but it is one rearrangement away from the questions that do appear.

trap.what: Adding two conditional probabilities that share a condition but whose events overlap, or adding probabilities with different conditions.
trap.why: P(.|B) obeys the addition rule only with the intersection subtracted, and two different conditions are two different measures.
trap.counterexample: With B = {2,4,6}: P({2,4}|B) = 2/3 and P({4,6}|B) = 2/3, but their union has probability 1, not 4/3. The intersection {4} carries 1/3, which is exactly the double count.

check.question: Given P(A|B) = 0.35, what is P(A^c|B)?
check.explanation: Inside the fixed condition B, A and A^c partition the space, so their conditional probabilities add to P(B|B) = 1.
